solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Access to go round Bill's track

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the access word encloses the bill

parts.note: recourse is access to a source of help
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a way to get around a track owned by a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name, but a bill is an account, and 'to go round' is the containment signal rather than a lap of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a track on which horses run.

clue.text: Stagger from film finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early means the film title stops one letter short

parts.note: Rocky is the 1976 boxing film

explanation.surface: Someone staggers out of a film that ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to sway or totter, as when staggering.

clue.text: Teach to run a posh estate

indicators.note: to run here means to go loose, so the letters of teach are rearranged

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone is taught to manage a grand country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French country house with its lands, a wine estate.

clue.text: Company must replace leader of organisation — that's the law!

indicators.note: must replace leader of means the first letter of the organisation word is swapped out

parts.note: an institution is an organisation

explanation.surface: A company must replace the head of an organisation, as the law requires.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitution is the body of fundamental law by which a state is governed.

clue.text: Corrupt trio rule in the future

definitions.note: an adjective sense: later, coming further on

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corrupt triumvirate will rule some day.
explanation.walkthrough: The less common sense is meant: lying beyond, subsequent, rather than hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulterior can mean further on or later in time, subsequent.

clue.text: Pressure finally breaks lock

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word breaks

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Pressure eventually breaks a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' looks like the verb doing the breaking, but supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain.

clue.text: Go and party

definitions.meaning: to have a go is to have a ..., an attempt

explanation.definitionFit: Both an attempt and a celebration can be called by this informal word.

clue.text: Stitch up Cockney dwelling south of area that's outstanding

indicators.note: south of in a down clue places the dwelling below the other pieces
up in a down clue means the stitch word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to stitch is to sew
a Cockney drops the H, so home becomes OME

explanation.surface: A Cockney home in the south is stitched up, and it is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome means amazing or remarkable, standing out.

clue.text: Preacher reportedly punctured car

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: punctured means holey, full of holes; a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: A preacher is said to have had his car punctured.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy roller is an evangelical preacher or worshipper given to frenzied displays.

clue.text: Bond's raced to find one of a group on the high street?

definitions.text: one of a group on the high street?

parts.note: a chain is a bond; the 's supplies the plural S
tore is the past of tear, to rush along

explanation.surface: James Bond races off to find something, perhaps a missing agent.
explanation.walkthrough: The high street is a British town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple retailer with branches in many towns is one shop belonging to a group.

clue.text: Most of posse fighting with this nasty piece of work could be hopeless

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the clue word may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram pool

indicators.note: most of the word posse means it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A villain so bad that any posse fighting alongside him would be doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: POSS (most of posse) together with the answer makes an anagram of HOPELESS; 'fighting with this' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy person, a cad.

clue.text: Book German genius missing first international

parts.note: the Franks were a Germanic people, so a Frank is a German

indicators.note: missing first means the opening one of the international letters is dropped

parts.note: Einstein is the byword for a genius

explanation.surface: A book about a German genius omits the first international.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's Gothic novel of 1818 is a famous book.

clue.text: Guy felt negative about clothes

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
clothes is a verb: the words felt negative wrap around the letters

explanation.surface: A man disliked what he was wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb, clothing TNEG inside felt negative; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gent, short for gentleman, is a man or fellow, like guy.

clue.text: Fund artist needing endless help for exhibition, ultimately

indicators.note: for signals that one piece takes the place of another in the artist's name

parts.note: Renoir was the French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word exhibition
endless means the help word loses its last letter

parts.note: to serve is to help

explanation.surface: An artist needs assistance to put on an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: SERV (serve without its end) replaces N, the last letter of exhibition, in RENOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store or supply to draw on, so a fund.

clue.text: Malevolent prince misrepresented debts

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters of prince are disordered

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A wicked prince lied about his debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernicious means harmful or destructive, with evil effect.

clue.text: Quite a different (and touching) expression for summer?

indicators.note: different says the letters of quite a are made into another arrangement

parts.note: on means touching, as in resting on

explanation.surface: A quite different, and moving, way of expressing the summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums, a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical statement with an equals sign is the kind of statement someone doing sums writes.

clue.text: Reveal nothing about European victor returning to follow United

indicators.note: to follow puts the following pieces after the letter for United

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: about means the nothing word goes around the other letters

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: returning means the European and victor letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A European winner going home after playing United reveals nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To unveil something is to uncover or disclose it.

clue.text: In the event of uprising, live somewhere warm

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the conditional word is read upwards

parts.note: if means in the event of
to reside is to live

explanation.surface: In the event of revolution, live somewhere safe and warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The area by the hearth is a cosy place near the heat.

clue.text: Tastier drink, reportedly a delicacy

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: tastier means nicer; tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A tastier drink is said to be a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without the R sounded, 'nicer tea' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or subtlety, a delicacy in the sense of fineness.

clue.text: Uri perhaps seen with a footballer

parts.note: Uri is a canton of Switzerland, an example

explanation.surface: Someone named Uri is seen with a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Cantona was a French forward famous at Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantona was a celebrated French football player.

clue.text: Parasites, unknown number, spot host

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: Someone spots parasites, uncountable numbers, on their host animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is the pub landlord, holder of a licence to sell alcohol, not an animal carrying parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee runs a licensed pub, so is its host to drinkers.

clue.text: Large number work to dismiss one in city

parts.note: a sea of faces is a large number

indicators.note: to dismiss one means the letter for one is sent away from the work word

parts.note: a title is a published work, as in a publisher's list
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A large workforce is told to lay off one person in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major city in Washington state.

clue.text: Conservative supports banker, flighty type

indicators.note: supports in a down clue places the Conservative below the banker

parts.note: a banker is a river, here the Fal in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A Tory backs a banker who is something of a flighty type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is the crossword river, one that has banks; the Fal flows through Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Attack deacon running to cuddle girl

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold in your arms, so the shuffled letters enclose the girl
running means the letters of deacon are set out of order

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A churchman runs off to cuddle a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' makes CONADE from deacon, which goes round ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonade is a sustained bombardment by heavy guns, a military attack.

clue.text: Spluttered, making argument

definitions.meaning: the past tense of spit, to splutter out words

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both spat out angrily and a minor row or tiff.

clue.text: Plan quietly to crush man with salty wife

indicators.note: to crush in a down clue puts the quiet letter on top of the man

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt in Genesis

explanation.surface: A quiet plan to crush a man with a sharp-tongued wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret scheme or plan.

clue.text: Tramps exposed source of music?

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagrants

explanation.surface: Tramps reveal where some music comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: Unexpected to receive Oscar for a Western

indicators.note: to receive Oscar for a means the letter is taken in where the a was

parts.note: accidental means unexpected or by chance
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Western film unexpectedly wins an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' is the adjective meaning of the West, not a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental means relating to the West, the opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Depression over new setback

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the depression word sits around the letter for new

parts.note: a sag is a dip or depression

explanation.surface: Depression returns after a new setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or hitch.

clue.text: Popular flier planned to avoid American in captivity

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a tern is a seabird, a flier

indicators.note: to avoid the American means that letter is left out of the planned word

parts.note: meant means intended or planned

explanation.surface: A popular bird was planned to avoid being caged in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is the confinement of people, especially in wartime, without trial.
